notes.text: The Harumiya shared boat only sails with 15 guests and you're 8, so strangers decide whether it runs. If Harumiya cancels, phone Funasei the same day (03-5479-2731, 10:00–19:00). Their shared boat sails from 2 guests.
Every Nozomi seat is reserved Dec 25–Jan 5: grab 8 seats in one car on smartEX the minute the window opens. The Kansai-Hiroshima pass does not cover this train.

Overnight bags only (the suitcases arrive at Garfield House this evening). Bring cash for Endo Sushi, warm layers for the river, and the original passports for every bar tonight. Check-in to door is only 30 minutes.

stops.summary: Last Osaka meal: market sushi plates, cash only, inside the wholesale fish market, then straight to Shin-Osaka.
stops.story: Endo Sushi sits inside Osaka's Central Wholesale Market, where the fish has travelled a few metres to your plate. You get five pieces per plate, and they keep coming as long as you keep ordering rounds. After a Round1 all-nighter it's the best hangover cure in Kansai.
how: Walk over from Kujō House (walk 20 min) or split into 2 taxis if legs are dead.
Order the 5-piece omakase plate and go again in rounds; you may be seated as two groups of 4.
Leave on time: Chūō line Awaza → Hommachi, then the Midōsuji line to Shin-Osaka, 11:43→11:53 (¥240, 39 min door to door).
tips: Cash only. No cards, no exceptions.
Recent reviewers quote ¥1,400–1,980 a plate, so budget for at least two each.
Use the spare time at Shin-Osaka for ekiben, beers and 551 Horai buta-man for the train.
wishes: We love to do it all
Legendary, not generic: nothing only there because it is on page one of every Tokyo or Kyoto itinerary, and no sit-down sightseeing filler between the big moments

stops.summary: Bullet train back to Tokyo: ekiben, beers, 551 buta-man and a nap, with Mt Fuji out the right-hand window.
stops.story: You'll sleep off Christmas at bullet-train speed with a lap full of Shin-Osaka ekiben. Wake up for Fuji on the right-hand side, rising over the brown winter fields.
how: Book 8 seats in one car on smartEX for the Nozomi around 12:30.
Buy ekiben, beers and 551 buta-man inside Shin-Osaka station before boarding.
At Tokyo, take the Marunouchi line to Shinjuku-gyoemmae, 15:30→15:46 (¥210), then walk.
tips: The pass doesn't cover this ride. Pay the full fare.
Keep the 551 bag sealed until the doors close, or the whole car will smell of buta-man.
stops.booking: smartEX; all seats are reserved Dec 25–Jan 5
wishes: We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country

stops.summary: 30 minutes flat: check in, bags down, warm layers on, passports in pockets, out the door at 16:30.
stops.story: Garfield House is home for the last Tokyo nights, and the suitcases from Osaka arrive here by TA-Q-BIN this evening. Don't wait in for them, because the boat won't wait for you.
how: Check in at 16:00 and confirm the host will take in the TA-Q-BIN suitcases.
Leave at 16:30: Toei Shinjuku line Shinjuku-sanchōme → Ichigaya, 16:54→16:59, then the JR Chūō-Sōbu local to Ryōgoku, 17:04→17:15 (¥380).
Walk to the Harumiya pier and be there by about 17:20–17:30.
tips: Arrive after the 17:45 gathering and you can't board and get no refund, so treat 16:30 as a hard deadline.
A taxi is 23 min, but Saturday traffic on a fireworks night is a gamble; the train is safer.

stops.summary: A tatami boat, unlimited drinks and the Odaiba fireworks over the water at 19:00. This is the night.
stops.story: A yakatabune is a lantern-lit wooden houseboat with tatami floors. Harumiya's shared boat sails 150 minutes past a glowing Skytree and out into Tokyo Bay. The Rainbow Fireworks go up at 19:00 and you'll be watching from the water with a drink in hand. You're 8 on a shared boat, so expect to be drinking with strangers by the end.
how: Be at Harumiya's Ryōgoku pier by 17:30 for the 17:45 gathering; it sails 18:00.
Book the Furisode set (¥13,200 pp) online and pay ahead by card.
When the fireworks start, go out on the roof deck: it's freezing up there, but the view is worth it.
tips: The shared boat only sails with 15 guests. If Harumiya cancels, book Funasei's shared yakatabune from Shinagawa (from ¥14,000 pp, phone 03-5479-2731).
Cancelling is free until 17:00, 11 days before boarding; 8 days out it costs 20%.
The fireworks are cancelled in bad weather. If it rains, the fallback is TJPW wrestling at Korakuen Hall (18:30).
stops.cost: ¥13,200 pp (Furisode set, tax incl.); Kachidoki set ¥15,400
stops.booking: Harumiya online, card in advance; shared boats from 2 guests
stops.hours: At the pier 17:30, gather 17:45, sail 18:00, back 20:30
wishes: A yakatabune dinner cruise with unlimited drinks on Sat 26 Dec, the night of the Odaiba fireworks
Be bold: prefer one-of-a-kind, local-run, hard-to-book and group-scale things, and name a safe fallback beside every hard-to-book thing

stops.summary: Nightcap in the San-chōme alleys: standing motsu-yaki, yakiton and highballs where Shinjuku locals drink.
stops.story: San-chōme is where Shinjuku goes to drink without the Kabukichō circus. The bars are smoky and shoulder-to-shoulder, and the skewers come off the grill as fast as you order. You're already full from the boat, so this round is about the drinks.
how: Sōbu local Ryōgoku → Yotsuya, then the Marunouchi line to Shinjuku-sanchōme (¥390, 41 min door to door).
Start at Nihon Saisei Sakaba (standing motsu-yaki), then Sanchōme no Yūta for yakiton.
Split 4+4 if a counter can't fit all eight of you.
tips: Tachinomi Arigatou pours until 5:00 if anyone refuses to go home.
Carry passports: the drinking age is 20 and bars check.
stops.hours: Nihon Saisei Sakaba 15:00–23:30; Sanchōme no Yūta 12:00–23:00; Tachinomi Arigatou 17:00–5:00
wishes: Karaoke (Manekineko, Big Echo, Karaokekan), arcades, izakaya and yokocho nights, standing bars, and the last-train problem solved properly

stops.summary: One party room, free-flow drinks, eight people screaming the same chorus. Out by 00:25 and walk home.
stops.story: Karaokekan's main Kabukichō branch never really closes, which makes it the safest bet in Shinjuku for a big room for 8 on a Saturday. Order free-flow, pick the songs everyone knows, and get through the setlist in one round.
how: Walk 9 min from San-chōme to Kabukichō.
Book a party room for 8 the same day by LINE or phone (03-5285-7007).
Add free-flow drinks; check the rate at the desk.
tips: The student rate needs a student ID, so bring one if you have it.
Walk past the Kabukichō touts and bar invites. Don't stop, don't answer.
It's a 14 min walk back to Garfield House afterwards.
stops.cost: About ¥2,000 pp (room and drinks; check the rate on the day)
stops.booking: Same day by LINE or phone 03-5285-7007
wishes: Karaoke (Manekineko, Big Echo, Karaokekan), arcades, izakaya and yokocho nights, standing bars, and the last-train problem solved properly
No nightclubs (a group rule from Plan C; ignore touts and bar invites in Kabukichō)
